tests.title: UPSC Prelims Mock Test 2 — GS Paper 1

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
questions.exp: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from which country?
questions.exp: Judicial Review, the power of courts to examine the constitutionality of laws, is borrowed from the United States Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions related to Anti-Defection Law?
questions.exp: The 10th Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985), contains anti-defection provisions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Rajya Sabha can delay a Money Bill for a maximum of how many days?
questions.exp: As per Article 110, the Rajya Sabha can only delay a Money Bill for a maximum of 14 days; it cannot reject or amend it.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was introduced by which Governor-General?
questions.exp: Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, under which a princely state would be annexed if the ruler died without a male heir.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Indian National Army (INA) was reorganized under whose leadership in 1943?
questions.exp: Subhash Chandra Bose reorganized the INA in 1943 in Singapore after taking leadership from Rash Behari Bose.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Simon Commission was boycotted by Indians mainly because:
questions.exp: The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted because it consisted entirely of British members with no Indian representation.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Which session of the Indian National Congress passed the 'Poorna Swaraj' resolution?
questions.exp: The Lahore Session of INC in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, passed the Poorna Swaraj (complete independence) resolution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate in India?
questions.exp: The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet (as the Yarlung Tsangpo) and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.exp: The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the highest peak located entirely within Indian territory?
questions.exp: Nanda Devi (7,816m) in Uttarakhand is the highest peak located entirely within India. Kangchenjunga is on the India-Nepal border.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Mawsynram, known for receiving the highest rainfall in the world, is located in which state?
questions.exp: Mawsynram in Meghalaya receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world, exceeding 11,000mm.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The term 'Stagflation' refers to a situation of:
questions.exp: Stagflation refers to a combination of economic stagnation (low growth, high unemployment) with high inflation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which committee recommended the establishment of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)?
questions.exp: SEBI was established in 1988 following recommendations associated with financial sector reforms, and was given statutory powers in 1992; the broader reform push came through the Narasimham Committee on financial sector reforms.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Fiscal Deficit is defined as:
opts: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
questions.exp: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - Total Receipts (excluding borrowings). It indicates how much the government needs to borrow.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Gini Coefficient' is used to measure:
questions.exp: The Gini Coefficient measures income or wealth inequality within a population, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Ramsar Convention is related to the conservation of:
questions.exp: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which gas is primarily responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer?
questions.exp: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are the primary cause of ozone layer depletion, addressed by the Montreal Protocol (1987).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Tiger was launched in India in which year?
questions.exp: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 by the Government of India to protect the tiger population.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following is a biodiversity hotspot in India?
questions.exp: The Western Ghats is one of the biodiversity hotspots overlapping India, along with the Eastern Himalaya, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which part of the human brain is responsible for maintaining balance and coordination?
questions.exp: The Cerebellum is responsible for maintaining balance, posture, and coordination of voluntary movements.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the south pole of the Moon on which date?
questions.exp: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander successfully soft-landed near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to achieve a lunar landing.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The element used in nuclear reactors as a moderator to slow down neutrons is typically:
questions.exp: Heavy water (deuterium oxide) is commonly used as a moderator in nuclear reactors to slow down fast neutrons.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: NITI Aayog replaced which earlier institution in January 2015?
questions.exp: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: India's first solar observation mission is named:
questions.exp: Aditya-L1, launched in September 2023, is India's first dedicated mission to study the Sun, positioned at the Lagrange point L1.

tests.title: UPSC Prelims Mock Test 3 — GS Paper 1

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution?
questions.exp: Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right but was removed by the 44th Amendment (1978) and made a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Election Commission of India is a:
questions.exp: The Election Commission of India is a Constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which amendment to the Constitution added the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble?
questions.exp: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The President of India can be impeached on the grounds of:
questions.exp: As per Article 61, the President can be impeached only on the ground of 'violation of the Constitution'.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the British and:
questions.exp: The Battle of Plassey was fought between Robert Clive's British forces and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, marking the beginning of British rule in India.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.exp: A.O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885 in Bombay.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The 'Champaran Satyagraha' (1917) led by Gandhi was related to the grievances of:
questions.exp: The Champaran Satyagraha was Gandhi's first major Satyagraha in India, addressing the grievances of indigo farmers forced into exploitative cultivation.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced which of the following?
questions.exp: The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced Provincial Autonomy, granting more powers to provinces compared to the earlier Diarchy under the 1919 Act.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Western Ghats are also known as:
questions.exp: The Western Ghats are also known as the Sahyadri range, running parallel to the western coast of India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to frequent flooding?
questions.exp: The Kosi river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its frequent and devastating floods in the region.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest coral reef system found in India?
questions.exp: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have the largest and most diverse coral reef system in India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Deccan Traps, known for fertile black soil, were formed due to:
questions.exp: The Deccan Traps were formed due to extensive volcanic activity millions of years ago, resulting in the fertile black (regur) soil ideal for cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India's primary tool to control inflation through interest rates is called:
questions.exp: The Repo Rate, the rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks, is the primary tool used to control inflation by influencing borrowing costs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: GST in India is a tax based on which principle?
questions.exp: GST is a destination-based tax, meaning tax revenue goes to the state where goods/services are consumed, not where they are produced.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which organization publishes the 'World Economic Outlook' report?
questions.exp: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) publishes the 'World Economic Outlook' report twice a year, analyzing global economic trends.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Disinvestment refers to:
opts: Government selling its stake in PSUs
questions.exp: Disinvestment refers to the government selling or liquidating its stake/assets in public sector undertakings (PSUs).

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is primarily aimed at:
questions.exp: The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty aimed at phasing out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances like CFCs.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a Greenhouse Gas?
questions.exp: Methane (CH4) is a potent greenhouse gas, along with CO2, N2O, and water vapor, contributing to global warming.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Silent Valley' movement was related to the protection of:
questions.exp: The Silent Valley movement (1970s-80s) was a successful environmental campaign to protect a tropical rainforest in Kerala from a proposed hydroelectric project.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India's first National Park, established in 1936, is:
questions.exp: Jim Corbett National Park (originally Hailey National Park) in Uttarakhand, established in 1936, is India's first national park.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which vaccine was developed indigenously in India for COVID-19?
questions.exp: Covaxin was developed indigenously by Bharat Biotech in collaboration with ICMR, while Covishield was manufactured under license from AstraZeneca.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The 'Green Revolution' in India during the 1960s was primarily associated with:
questions.exp: The Green Revolution introduced high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, along with increased use of fertilizers and irrigation, significantly boosting food grain production.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: INS Vikrant, commissioned in 2022, is India's first:
questions.exp: INS Vikrant, commissioned in September 2022, is India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: The G20 Summit 2023 was hosted by India in which city?
questions.exp: India hosted the G20 Summit 2023 in New Delhi, with the theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future).

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: Which scheme aims to provide free electricity up to 300 units to households via rooftop solar?
questions.exp: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana aims to provide free electricity up to 300 units monthly to households through rooftop solar installations.

tests.title: UPSC Prelims Mock Test 4 — GS Paper 1

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which Article empowers the President to dissolve the Lok Sabha?
questions.exp: Article 85 empowers the President to summon, prorogue Parliament, and dissolve the Lok Sabha, acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'Basic Structure' doctrine of the Constitution was propounded in which landmark case?
questions.exp: The Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala (1973) case established the Basic Structure doctrine, ruling that Parliament cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.exp: The President can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from persons with special knowledge in art, literature, science, and social service.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which of the following writs is issued to compel a public authority to perform a duty it has failed to perform?
questions.exp: Mandamus, meaning 'we command', is issued to direct a public official or authority to perform a duty they are legally obligated to perform.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The 'Pitt's India Act' of 1784 established which body to control the East India Company?
questions.exp: Pitt's India Act, 1784 established a Board of Control in Britain to oversee the East India Company's political and administrative affairs.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Who was the leader of the 1857 revolt at Jhansi?
questions.exp: Rani Lakshmibai led the revolt at Jhansi during the 1857 uprising, fighting against British forces until her death in battle.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The 'Mountbatten Plan' of June 1947 proposed:
questions.exp: The Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) proposed the partition of British India into India and Pakistan, leading to independence on 15 August 1947.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Which newspaper was edited by Bal Gangadhar Tilak to spread nationalist ideas?
questions.exp: Bal Gangadhar Tilak edited 'Kesari' (in Marathi) and 'Mahratta' (in English) to spread nationalist sentiment among Indians.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 'Radcliffe Line' demarcates the border between India and:
questions.exp: The Radcliffe Line, drawn in 1947 by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, demarcates the border between India and Pakistan (and subsequently Bangladesh).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which state has the longest coastline in India?
questions.exp: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states, approximately 1,600 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, is located in which two countries?
questions.exp: The Sundarbans, known for the Royal Bengal Tiger, spans across India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh, forming the world's largest mangrove forest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Loktak Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, is located in:
questions.exp: Loktak Lake, famous for its floating islands called 'phumdis', is located in Manipur.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which body regulates insurance companies in India?
questions.exp: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) regulates and promotes the insurance industry in India.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Phillips Curve' represents the relationship between:
questions.exp: The Phillips Curve depicts the inverse relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment in an economy.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a Direct Tax in India?
questions.exp: Income Tax is a Direct Tax, levied directly on the income of individuals and companies. GST, Excise, and Customs are Indirect Taxes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: NABARD primarily provides credit and financial support for:
questions.exp: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development), established in 1982, is the apex institution for agriculture and rural development financing.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) primarily aimed to:
questions.exp: The Kyoto Protocol was the first international treaty committing developed countries to legally binding greenhouse gas emission reduction targets.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which Indian wildlife sanctuary is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion?
questions.exp: Gir National Park in Gujarat is the only natural habitat in the world for the Asiatic Lion.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The 'Paris Agreement' (2015) aims to limit global temperature rise to:
questions.exp: The Paris Agreement aims to limit global average temperature increase to well below 2°C, pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Biomagnification refers to:
opts: Increase in pollutant concentration up the food chain
questions.exp: Biomagnification refers to the progressive increase in concentration of toxic substances (like DDT) at successive levels of the food chain.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Which Indian scientist is credited with discovering the Raman Effect?
questions.exp: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect in 1928, related to the scattering of light, for which he won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The 'Gaganyaan' mission is India's first:
questions.exp: Gaganyaan is India's first crewed human spaceflight mission, aimed at sending Indian astronauts into low Earth orbit.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Stem cells are characterized by their ability to:
questions.exp: Stem cells have the unique ability to differentiate into various specialized cell types in the body, making them important in regenerative medicine.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India is the position created to:
opts: Provide single-point military advice to the government
questions.exp: The post of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), created in 2019, provides single-point military advice to the Defence Minister and coordinates among the three services.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: India's Agnipath/Agniveer recruitment scheme, launched in 2022, applies to which sector?
questions.exp: The Agnipath scheme, launched in 2022, introduced a short-term recruitment model for soldiers (Agniveers) in the Indian Armed Forces.
